newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: American reappointed as UN development chief.
newsitem.headline: American reappointed as UN development chief.

text.p: James Gustave Speth, an American, was nominated by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Friday for another four years as head of the U.N. Development Programme, the largest U.N. specialised agency.
Annan, in a letter, asked the General Assembly to confirm the nomination of Speth for a second term beginning on July 16. Confirmation by the assembly is considered a formality.
Speth was originally proposed for the job by President Bill Clinton in 1993, and was the senior environmental official in former President Jimmy Carter's White House.
UNDP distributed close to $1 billion a year to developing countries to combat poverty and give technical assistance.
The United States holds the directorship of two other U.N. agencies: The U.N. Children's Fund, UNICEF, headed by Carol Bellamy, and the World Food Programme headed by Catherine Bertini.
